sentences.text:
This Appeal Coming On For Further Hearing, This
Day, Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:

Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice T.G. Shivashankare Gowda
 Oral Judgment

In this appeal, the petitioners are challenging the judgment dated 27.11.2013 passed in MVC.No.52/2007 by the Principal Civil Judge and JMFC, Kolar (in short 'the Tribunal').
2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties herein are referred as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

Brief facts of the case are, on 08.09.1997, the husband of petitioner No.1 and father of petitioner No.2 by name K. Suguna Murthy, the deceased, as per the instructions of his employer-respondent No.1 was traveling in the lorry bearing registration No. AP-02-T- 0789 (in short 'Andhra lorry') for unloading groundnut extraction at Bengaluru.

At about 7:00 p.m near Yalakamakalapalli bus stand at NH-7, the said lorry dashed against another lorry bearing registration No. MH-04/h-3205 (in short 'Maharashtra lorry') coming from the opposite direction, as a result of which the deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to death at the spot.

The petitioners seeking grant of compensation of `10,00,000/- have approached the Tribunal under Section 163A of the Motor Smt Manjula vs Sri K Ramachari on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48763165/
2 Vehicles Act, 1988 ('the Act' for short).

entities.text: Motor Smt Manjula vs Sri K Ramachari on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claim was opposed by both the Insurance Companies.

The Tribunal after taking the evidence and hearing both the parties has assessed compensation of `2,20,000/- and directed the owners of both lorries to pay compensation equally and dismissed the claim NC: 2024:KHC:37842 petition against the Insurance Companies.

Pleading inadequacy,
seeking enhancement and challenging the order of the dismissal of the claim against Insurance Companies, the petitioners are before this Court.

4. Heard the arguments of Smt. Suguna R. Reddy learned counsel for the petitioners, Sr. K.N.
Srinivasa, learned counsel for the Insurance Company of the Andhra lorry and Sri. E.I. Sanmathi,
learned counsel for the Insurance Company of the Maharashtra lorry.
5.

It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the deceased was employee under respondent No.1, they have filed petition for grant of compensation under the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 before the Commissioner.
For the reason of non- establishment of relationship, the claim petition came to be dismissed.
Without any alternative, the petitioners have filed the claim under Section 163A of the Act.

5.1. It is also contended that the accident is not in dispute, the deceased was the inmate of the Andhra NC: 2024:KHC:37842 lorry, policy of insurance covers the risk of the deceased irrespective of whether coolie or inmate of the lorry.
The insurer of the Andhra lorry is bound to indemnify the owner.
Inspite of furnishing particulars of the insurance policy, the insurer of the Maharashtra lorry has not produced the insurance policy.
By drawing adverse inference, the insurer of the Maharashtra lorry is to be directed to pay the compensation.

5.2. It is further contended that, the claim made by the driver and cleaner of the Andhra lorry before the Tribunal at Andhra Pradesh was satisfied by the Insurance Company and only with respect to the petitioners they are blowing hot and cold.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company of the Andhra lorry has contended that,
the deceased was non fair paying passenger in the lorry, he was not an employee employed by the respondent No.1.
For this reason, claim petition filed before Workmen's Compensation Commissioner came to be dismissed.
The NC: 2024:KHC:37842 deceased being a non-fare paying passenger, the policy does not cover his risk.

The policy covers only non-fare paying employee No.1,
paid drivers or workmen No.6.
When there is no coverage of policy, there is no liability on the part of the insurer to indemnify the insured.

7. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company of the Maharashtra lorry has contended that the policy of insurance mentioned in the cause title of the claim petition was not issued by the Insurance Company.

No evidence is placed by the petitioners to establish the existence of policy of insurance in respect of Maharashtra lorry and therefore, the Insurance Company has no liability to indemnify the insured.
The petitioners are required to go against the Andhra lorry only.
8. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the parties and perused the records.

3 9.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The material on record goes to show that the claim made by the driver and cleaner of the Andhra lorry NC: 2024:KHC:37842 was already satisfied by the insurer of Andhra lorry and thereby the accident came to be admitted.
At the time of accident the deceased was inmate of the Andhra lorry.

The petitioners have approached the Commissioner of Workman's Compensation, Kolar in WCA/FC.No.31/2000 and Commissioner as per the order dated 07.02.2003 dismissed the claim petition for non-proving of relationship.
Ex.R.1 is the certified copy of the said order.
In view of the same, two points that arisen for consideration of this Court are, the quantum of compensation and liability on the part of the insurers to indemnify to the insured.
10. As regarding quantum of compensation is concerned, postmortem report points out the age of the deceased as 50.
Election identification card of the deceased is produced as per Ex.P.8.
On its perusal, it is pertinent to note that as on 01.01.1996, the age of the deceased was 43 years.
The accident was one year nine months thereafter, then the correct age of the deceased has to be taken at 45 instead of 50.
As per schedule - 2 NC: 2024:KHC:37842 of Section 163A of the Act, applicable multiplier is 15.
The accident is of the year 1997 the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at `2,000/- p.m, and 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal expenses and applicable multiplier is 15.

Then loss of dependency will be Rs.2000/- - Rs.666/- (1/3) = Rs.1334/- X 12 X 15 =
Rs.2,40,120/-.
11.
Under the structured formula loss of consortium to the wife at `5,000/-, funeral expenses at `2,000/-, loss of estate at `2,500/- has to be assessed.
Thereby the compensation under conventional heads comes to `9,500/-.
Total compensation comes to `2,49,620/- as against `2,20,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Thereby enhancement of `29,620/-, it is just compensation that the petitioners are entitled to, under the facts and circumstances of the case.

12. As regarding liability is concerned, it is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners that Insurance Company has collected premium for one non-fare paying passenger, policy is a B- NC: 2024:KHC:37842 Comprehensive policy and it covers the risk of inmates of the lorry apart from the driver and the workman.
The insurer cannot avoid its liability to indemnify the insured.

13. It is the argument of the learned counsel for the Insurance Company of Andhra lorry that the premium of Rs.50/- was collected to cover the risk of one non-fare paying employee, not the non-fare paying passenger.
Hence, the contract of policy does not contemplate coverage of risk of the deceased in the said lorry, who is a gratuitous passenger.
The claim of the petitioners that the deceased was an employee under the owner has been negatived by the Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation, which is not challenged by them.
14. The prosecution papers indicate charge sheet was filed against the driver of the Maharashtra lorry.

The IMV report is also placed as per Ex.P4,
- 10 - Smt Manjula vs Sri K Ramachari on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48763165/
4 NC: 2024:KHC:37842 which points out the policy particulars in respect of the Maharashtra lorry.
Respondent No.4, the insurer of the Maharashtra lorry, in the objection statement specifically denied that no such policy was issued.

Under such circumstances, since the claim is under Section 163A of the Act, the petitioners are entitled to claim compensation from the owners of both vehicles.
15. Ex.R2 is the B-Comprehensive policy and it covers the risk of third parties.

Hence, it is relevant to refer to Section 149(1) of the Act, which reads thus:
"149. Duty of insurers to satisfy judgments and awards against persons insured in respect of third party risks.--(1) If, after a certificate of insurance has been issued under sub-section (3) of section 147 in favour of the person by whom a policy has been effected, judgment or award in respect of any such liability as Is required to be covered by a policy under clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 147 (being a liability covered by the terms of the policy) '[or under the provisions of section 163A] is obtained against any person insured by the policy, then, notwithstanding that the insurer may be entitled to avoid or cancel or may have avoided or cancelled the policy, the insurer shall, subject to the provisions of this section, pay to the person entitled to the benefit of the decree any sum not exceeding the sum assured payable thereunder, as if he were the judgment debtor, in respect of the liability, together with any amount payable in respect of costs and any sum - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:37842 payable in respect of interest on that sum by virtue of any enactment relating to interest on judgments."
16.
Now the petitioners have obtained the award under Section 163A of the Act.
They are the third parties to the policy of insurance.
Under such circumstances, it is the duty of the insurer to satisfy the judgment and award against the persons insured in respect of third party risk.
The policy of insurance was issued under Section 147(3) of the Act.

In view of Section 149(1) of the Act,
notwithstanding that the insurer may be entitled to avoid its liability, he shall pay the compensation.
Hence, the Insurance Company cannot avoid its liability fastened under Section 163A of the Act and it has to indemnify the insured/owner of the Andhra lorry.
The actionable negligence is against the driver of Maharashtra lorry and for this reason, he was charge sheeted.
The Insurance Company has to satisfy the award and work out its remedy to recover - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:37842 the compensation from the owner and insurer of the Maharashtra lorry.
